Downy mildew:
🔴 IMMEDIATE ACTION
• Remove all infected leaves immediately
• Cut 2-3 inches above the visible infection area
• Destroy leaves completely (do not compost)
• Seal in a plastic bag before disposal

💨 IMPROVE AIR CIRCULATION
• Prune lower leaves to increase airflow
• Increase spacing between plants
• Use ceiling or portable fans in enclosed spaces
• Ensure 15-20 cm minimum distance between plant canopies

💧 WATER MANAGEMENT
• Switch to drip irrigation system
• Water soil directly - never wet the foliage
• Water early in the morning
• Allow water on leaves to dry within 2-3 hours maximum

🌡️ ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL
• Reduce humidity to 65-70% (use dehumidifier if needed)
• Keep daytime temperature between 22-25°C
• Avoid cool, wet conditions overnight
• Ensure good ventilation at all times

💊 CHEMICAL TREATMENT
• Apply copper-based fungicide (Bordeaux mixture 1%)
• Or use sulfur spray (80% wettable powder)
• Spray every 7-10 days for 3-4 weeks
• Rotate between different fungicide types to prevent resistance
• Always follow product instructions for safety

🛡️ PREVENTIVE MEASURES
• Continue monitoring for new symptoms
• Apply preventive fungicide every 2-3 weeks
• Monitor for 4-6 weeks after initial treatment
• Inspect both upper and lower leaf surfaces regularly

⚠️ POST-TREATMENT
• Do not harvest leaves for 2 weeks after last treatment
• Disinfect all pruning tools with 70% alcohol
• Wash hands thoroughly after handling plants
• Avoid spreading to other plants through tools or hands
Healthy:
✅ GREAT NEWS!
• Your agarwood leaf shows no disease symptoms
• Disease identification: Negative
• Overall leaf health status: Excellent
• Continue with current care routine

💧 WATERING SCHEDULE
• Maintain consistent soil moisture (60-70%)
• Water when top 2-3 cm of soil feels dry
• Use room temperature water
• Avoid waterlogging - ensure proper drainage

☀️ LIGHTING CONDITIONS
• Provide 6-8 hours of indirect sunlight daily
• Avoid direct harsh afternoon sun
• Rotate plant every 2-3 days for even growth
• Use grow lights if natural light is insufficient

🌡️ TEMPERATURE & HUMIDITY
• Maintain temperature between 20-28°C
• Keep humidity at 70-80% (use humidifier if needed)
• Avoid sudden temperature fluctuations
• Protect from cold drafts and heating vents

🔍 REGULAR INSPECTION
• Inspect leaves weekly for early disease signs
• Check both upper and lower leaf surfaces
• Look for spots, discoloration, or unusual marks
• Act quickly if any symptoms appear

🧼 HYGIENE & SANITATION
• Sanitize pruning tools with 70% alcohol before use
• Wash hands after handling plants
• Remove fallen leaves promptly
• Keep work area clean and sanitized

🌱 NUTRITION SUPPORT
• Apply balanced fertilizer (NPK 10-10-10) monthly
• Or use organic compost every 2-3 months
• This boosts plant immunity against diseases
• Follow dosage instructions carefully
Mealy bugs:
🔴 CRITICAL FIRST STEP
• Isolate infected plant immediately
• Move at least 2-3 meters away from other plants
• Keep isolated for minimum 4-6 weeks
• This prevents spread to your entire collection

✋ MANUAL REMOVAL METHOD
• Use cotton swabs or soft brush
• Dip in 70% isopropyl alcohol
• Gently rub each visible mealy bug and white masses
• Pay attention to leaf joints and stems - bugs hide there

🔄 REMOVAL SCHEDULE
• Repeat manual removal every 3-4 days
• Continue for 2-3 weeks
• Check both sides of leaves thoroughly
• Use magnifying glass to inspect hidden areas

💊 SPRAY TREATMENT
• Apply neem oil solution (2% concentrate)
• Or use insecticidal soap spray
• Spray both upper and lower leaf surfaces thoroughly
• Repeat every 5-7 days for at least 3 applications

🔀 ROTATION OF TREATMENTS
• Alternate between different pesticide types
• This prevents mealy bugs from building resistance
• Try: Week 1-2 (neem oil) → Week 3-4 (soap spray) → Week 5-6 (another option)
• Never use same product for more than 2 consecutive weeks

🔍 DETAILED INSPECTION
• Check leaf axils (where leaves connect)
• Inspect along stems and branches
• Look inside leaf crevices
• Use magnifying glass for tiny insects
• Mark treated areas to track progress

🌡️ ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
• Avoid high nitrogen fertilizer (promotes soft growth)
• Maintain moderate humidity (65-75%)
• Ensure good air circulation
• Maintain temperature 20-25°C
• These conditions reduce pest severity

📊 MONITORING PERIOD
• Continue treatment for 4-6 weeks minimum
• If reinfestation occurs, restart isolation
• Keep detailed notes on treatment dates
• Consider destroying if severe after 6 weeks of treatment
Mosaic Viruses:
⚠️ CRITICAL WARNING - NO CURE AVAILABLE
• Mosaic viruses CANNOT be treated or cured
• Once established, virus remains in plant permanently
• No antiviral chemicals are effective
• Plant cannot recover - disease is permanent

🚫 IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED
• Remove and destroy the entire infected plant
• Do NOT attempt to save it with treatment
• Dispose in sealed bag to prevent spread
• Do not compost - virus survives in soil

🧼 PREVENT TRANSMISSION
• Clean all tools with 10% bleach solution
• Or use 70% isopropyl alcohol
• Wash hands thoroughly before touching other plants
• Disinfect work surfaces and pots

🦟 VECTOR CONTROL (INSECT CONTROL)
• Aphids spread mosaic viruses between plants
• Control with insecticidal soap or neem oil
• Spray every 5-7 days to eliminate vectors
• Monitor surrounding plants closely
• Reduce vector population by 90%+

🔍 SURROUNDING PLANT INSPECTION
• Check all nearby plants weekly
• Look for mottling (irregular coloring)
• Watch for leaf distortion or curling
• Note any color patches or striping
• Any symptoms = immediate removal needed

⏸️ ISOLATION PROTOCOL
• Keep surrounding plants isolated for 2-3 months
• Maintain 1+ meter distance between plants
• Do not move plants between areas
• Remove any volunteer or weed seedlings
• These can harbor hidden virus

📋 NEW PLANT QUARANTINE
• Always quarantine new plant purchases
• Keep separate for 4 weeks minimum
• Inspect carefully before adding to collection
• Use different tools for quarantined plants
• Verify health before placement

💡 PREVENTION IS ONLY OPTION
• Maintain strict plant hygiene always
• Use disease-free planting material only
• Never reuse soil from infected plants
• Avoid overhead watering (reduces insect-mediated spread)
• Sanitation is your best defense against viruses
Translucent lesion:
🔴 IMMEDIATE REMOVAL
• Remove affected leaves immediately
• Cut at the petiole (where leaf connects to stem)
• Place in sealed plastic bag for disposal
• Do NOT leave on ground or near plant
• Work carefully to avoid spore spread

💧 WATERING ADJUSTMENT
• Reduce watering frequency immediately
• Water only when soil is 60-70% dry
• Switch to drip irrigation if possible
• AVOID wetting the foliage completely
• Apply water only at soil level

💨 HUMIDITY MANAGEMENT
• Decrease humidity to 65-70% (use fan)
• Eliminate standing water around plant
• Ensure air movement around all leaves
• Do NOT use misting or foliar spray
• Good air circulation prevents disease spread

☀️ INCREASE LIGHT EXPOSURE
• Increase to 6-8 hours of indirect sunlight daily
• Good light helps plant recover faster
• Improves leaf photosynthesis activity
• Boosts plant immune system significantly
• Prevents disease from progressing further

🌱 VERIFY SOIL DRAINAGE
• Check that soil mixture drains well
• Ideal mix: 40% perlite + 40% potting soil + 20% sand
• Test by watering - water should drain in 2-3 minutes
• Soggy soil causes rapid lesion spread
• Repot if drainage is poor

💊 FUNGICIDE APPLICATION
• Apply copper fungicide weekly
• Or use sulfur-based fungicide
• Spray for 3-4 consecutive weeks
• Use preventive dose, not high concentration
• Always follow product instructions

🔍 ROOT INSPECTION
• Gently remove plant from pot
• Inspect entire root system carefully
• Healthy roots: White or light brown, firm
• Diseased roots: Dark brown, mushy, foul smell
• If rotting: Repot immediately in fresh sterile soil

📊 RECOVERY TIMELINE
• Expect 2-4 weeks for new healthy leaves
• Lesions should stop spreading within 1 week
• Monitor daily for new symptoms
• If lesions continue spreading despite treatment = possible bacterial co-infection

⚠️ ADVANCED MANAGEMENT
• If lesions spread rapidly = apply bactericide too
• Reduce fertilizer - plant needs recovery time
• Keep separate from other plants for 6 weeks
• Continue inspection for full 6 weeks
• Note: Some leaf damage is permanent but plant can recover
Uncertain:
❌ IMAGE NOT RECOGNIZED
• The uploaded image is unclear
• Or does not match training data patterns
• Please capture a new photo and try again
• Follow guidelines below for better results

📸 PHOTOGRAPHY GUIDELINES
• Use natural lighting (NOT flash photography)
• Ensure leaf is in sharp focus
• Photograph from directly above the leaf
• Avoid shadows on the leaf surface
• Clean camera lens before taking photo

🍃 LEAF SELECTION
• Choose a single affected leaf if possible
• Select the most clearly diseased part
• Show both healthy and diseased areas for comparison
• Avoid blurred or corrupted backgrounds
• Do NOT include multiple leaves in one image

🧹 PREPARE THE LEAF
• Gently clean the leaf with soft cloth
• Remove any dust or debris
• Ensure the entire leaf surface is visible
• Include stem/petiole in photo
• Make leaf prominent in the frame (70%+ of image)

🖼️ IMAGE COMPOSITION
• Use plain, contrasting background (white works best)
• Place leaf against background for clarity
• Ensure no shadows across the leaf
• Position for maximum detail visibility
• Leave 10-20% margin around leaf edges

📐 IMAGE SPECIFICATIONS
• Minimum size: 224×224 pixels
• Recommended: 500×500 pixels or larger
• Preferred format: JPG or PNG
• File size: Less than 5 MB
• Try different formats if JPG doesn't work

🔄 ANGLE VARIATION
• If first image unclear, try different angles
• Top view (leaf directly from above)
• Bottom view (showing underside details)
• Side angle (showing leaf profile)
• Different angles may reveal details better

✅ VERIFICATION
• Confirm it's an Agarwood (agar) leaf
• This model is specifically trained for agarwood only
• If unsure about plant species = verify with botanist first
• Once confirmed as agarwood = try retaking photo
• Model accuracy improves with clear leaf images
